sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A Times investigation has found that doctors are increasingly performing unnecessary medical procedures that generate huge profits while often harming patients.
sentences.zh: 《时报》的一项调查发现，医生越来越多地进行不必要的医疗程序，这些程序产生了巨额利润，同时往往对患者造成伤害。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Katie Thomas on the forces driving this emerging and troubling trend in American health care and the story of one family caught in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯蒂·托马斯将讲述推动美国医疗保健领域这一新兴且令人不安的趋势背后的力量，以及一个陷入其中的家庭的故事。

sentences.en: It's Monday, February 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月19日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Katie, tell me about this investigation.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯蒂，跟我讲讲这项调查吧。

sentences.en: So I am a health care reporter who writes about the kind of intersection of health care and money.
sentences.zh: 我是一名医疗保健记者，主要撰写关于医疗保健与金钱交汇点的内容。

sentences.en: And I was working with two other colleagues, Sarah Cliff and Jessica Silver-Greenberg.
sentences.zh: 我当时和另外两位同事萨拉·克利夫和杰西卡·西尔弗-格林伯格一起工作。

sentences.en: And together, the three of us had long been interested in, are the medical procedures and
sentences.zh: 我们三个人长期以来一直对以下问题很感兴趣：医疗程序以及

sentences.en: the tests and other things that we get when we go to the doctor or into a hospital, are they always necessary?
sentences.zh: 我们在看医生或去医院时接受的检查和其他事情，它们总是必要的吗？

sentences.en: But what we were really interested in exploring was not just are these procedures and are these tests, et cetera, are they necessary?
sentences.zh: 但我们真正有兴趣探讨的不仅仅是这些程序和检查等是否必要？

sentences.en: But in some situations, could they actually be harmful to patients?
sentences.zh: 而是在某些情况下，它们实际上会对患者造成伤害吗？

sentences.en: And so that's what we decided to try and take a look at.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们决定尝试去了解的。

sentences.en: And so we had gotten started in our reporting when we got a tip.
sentences.zh: 当我们接到一个线索时，我们的报道刚刚开始。

sentences.en: And it was from a mom in Boise, Idaho.
sentences.zh: 线索来自爱达荷州博伊西的一位妈妈。

sentences.en: And her name was Lauren Lavelle.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫劳伦·拉韦尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: And my colleague Jessica Silver-Greenberg and I went to her house to meet with her.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事杰西卡·西尔弗-格林伯格去了她家拜访她。

sentences.en: And where does her story start?
sentences.zh: 她的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: I am a mom of two.
sentences.zh: 我是两个孩子的妈妈。

sentences.en: I live in Boise.
sentences.zh: 我住在博伊西。

sentences.en: My daughter June is four and I have a 17-month-old Flora.
sentences.zh: 我的女儿朱恩四岁，我还有一个17个月大的弗洛拉。

sentences.en: Her story starts when Lauren gets pregnant with her daughter June.
sentences.zh: 她的故事始于劳伦怀上女儿朱恩的时候。

sentences.en: So by the time we got pregnant with June, November of 2018, about eight months after we had the miscarriage, I think I was just more hesitant and nervous than anything.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们怀上朱恩时，即2018年11月，大约在我们流产八个月后，我觉得自己比什么都犹豫和紧张。

sentences.en: Lauren and her husband had had trouble conceiving.
sentences.zh: 劳伦和她的丈夫在怀孕方面遇到过困难。

sentences.en: And so they were so happy when they learned that they were going to have June.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们得知将要拥有朱恩时，他们感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: And like both first-time parents, they were also a little bit nervous.
sentences.zh: 像所有第一次当父母的人一样，他们也感到有点紧张。

sentences.en: But being type A and super prepared, I did all my homework.
sentences.zh: 但作为A型人格且超级准备充分的人，我做了所有的功课。

sentences.en: We hired a doula.
sentences.zh: 我们雇了一个导乐。

sentences.en: I wanted an epidural.
sentences.zh: 我想要硬膜外麻醉。

sentences.en: Having a natural child birth absolutely was not for me.
sentences.zh: 自然分娩绝对不适合我。

sentences.en: And Lauren is very organized.
sentences.zh: 劳伦非常有条理。

sentences.en: She's always on top of everything.
sentences.zh: 她总是把一切都安排得井井有条。

sentences.en: And she makes all sorts of plans.
sentences.zh: 她制定了各种各样的计划。

sentences.en: And she gets a lot of different providers lined up ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 她提前联系好了许多不同的服务提供商。

sentences.en: I didn't know anything about breastfeeding, like zero things.
sentences.zh: 我对母乳喂养一无所知，简直是零。

sentences.en: Including one that she has hired to help her with breastfeeding.
sentences.zh: 其中包括她雇来帮助她进行母乳喂养的人。

sentences.en: Where did you find out about her?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里知道她的？

sentences.en: So I asked our doula for a list of recommendations.
sentences.zh: 我向我们的导乐索取了一份推荐名单。

sentences.en: And she gave me a very short liSt.
sentences.zh: 她给了我一张很短的名单。

sentences.en: At the time, there were very few lactation consultants in the Valley.
sentences.zh: 当时，山谷里的哺乳顾问非常少。

sentences.en: And Melanie was one of them.
sentences.zh: 梅兰妮就是其中之一。

sentences.en: She ended up deciding to work with Melanie Henstrom, who is a local lactation consultant in Boise.
sentences.zh: 她最终决定与梅兰妮·亨斯特姆合作，后者是博伊西当地的一位哺乳顾问。

sentences.en: She sold this package at the time.
sentences.zh: 她当时出售这个套餐。

sentences.en: I don't know if she still did.
sentences.zh: 我不知道她现在是否还在这样做。

sentences.en: But it was like prenatal visit, breastfeeding class.
sentences.zh: 但这就像产前访问、母乳喂养课程。

sentences.en: And then she'll come to the hospital and help you latch.
sentences.zh: 然后她会去医院帮你让婴儿含乳。

sentences.en: And then she'll come to the house a couple times after.
sentences.zh: 然后她会去家里好几次。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, this sounds perfect.
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，听起来很完美。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: You know, I'm covered there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这方面我不用担心了。

sentences.en: So one week after her due date, she gives birth.
sentences.zh: 所以在预产期后一周，她生下了孩子。

sentences.en: And it was a difficult labor.
sentences.zh: 这是一次艰难的生产。

sentences.en: It took 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 花了24个小时。

sentences.en: Lauren was completely exhausted.
sentences.zh: 劳伦精疲力竭。

sentences.en: But once June arrived, the family was very, very excited to have her.
sentences.zh: 但一旦朱恩降生，全家人都为她的到来感到非常非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And I remember June coming out and that surreal feeling you have when you see your first baby for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我记得朱恩出来时那种超现实的感觉，当你第一次看到你的第一个孩子时。

sentences.en: Like, oh my God, like there's a baby in the room.
sentences.zh: 就像，哦天哪，房间里有个婴儿。

sentences.en: And June was a healthy baby, but she was having trouble breastfeeding.
sentences.zh: 朱恩是个健康的婴儿，但她在母乳喂养方面遇到了困难。

sentences.en: She would not latch.
sentences.zh: 她不肯含乳。

sentences.en: Like, she wouldn't even attempt.
sentences.zh: 就像，她甚至不肯尝试。

sentences.en: She would scream.
sentences.zh: 她会尖叫。

sentences.en: It was the only time she ever cried if you tried to make her breastfeed.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图让她母乳喂养，这是她唯一哭泣的时候。

sentences.en: And so as her pediatrician was making the rounds, they noticed that June was having trouble and said that June's tongue is really tight.
sentences.zh: 因此，当她的儿科医生查房时，他们注意到朱恩遇到了困难，并说朱恩的舌系带太紧了。

sentences.en: We can clip it if you'd like.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，我们可以剪开它。

sentences.en: And that they could clip it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以剪开它。

sentences.en: What does that mean exactly, Katie, clipping her tongue?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，剪舌系带到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: What it means is that there's a small percentage of babies whose tongue is very tightly tethered to the bottom of their mouth.
sentences.zh: 意思是有一小部分婴儿的舌头与口腔底部的连接非常紧密。

sentences.en: And for a very small percentage of babies, their tongue is almost tied so tightly down that they can't nurse well.
sentences.zh: 对于极少数婴儿来说，他们的舌头系得太紧，以至于无法很好地吸吮。

sentences.en: So it makes breastfeeding very difficult if a baby has a tongue like this.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果婴儿有这样的舌头，母乳喂养就会变得非常困难。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you bottle feed your baby, the baby can basically adjust and make do.
sentences.zh: 如果你用奶瓶喂养婴儿，婴儿基本上可以适应并凑合。

sentences.en: But if you want to breastfeed, some babies have trouble basically latching on to their mother when they don't have that tongue motion.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想母乳喂养，一些婴儿在没有这种舌头运动的情况下，很难含住母亲的乳头。

sentences.en: And so some version of clipping these tongue ties has been done for centuries.
sentences.zh: 因此，几个世纪以来，人们一直在进行某种版本的剪舌系带手术。

sentences.en: Midwives have been doing it.
sentences.zh: 助产士一直在这样做。

sentences.en: Pediatricians do it.
sentences.zh: 儿科医生也在做。

sentences.en: And traditionally what it's been is a very quick snip right underneath the tongue just to loosen up the tongue.
sentences.zh: 传统上，这是在舌头下方快速剪一下，以放松舌头。

sentences.en: And traditionally that procedure is extremely straightforward.
sentences.zh: 传统上，这个过程非常简单。

sentences.en: There's little to no follow-up care.
sentences.zh: 几乎不需要后续护理。

sentences.en: And basically the baby naturally heals as it learns to breastfeed.
sentences.zh: 婴儿在学会母乳喂养的同时自然痊愈。

sentences.en: And so we said, okay, you know, they explained that it was completely painless.
sentences.zh: 所以我们说，好吧，你知道，他们解释说这完全是无痛的。

sentences.en: They do it with scissors.
sentences.zh: 他们用剪刀做这件事。

sentences.en: She wouldn't even feel it.
sentences.zh: 她甚至都不会感觉到。

sentences.en: And all of that was true.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是真的。

sentences.en: They clipped it.
sentences.zh: 他们剪开了。

sentences.en: I don't even think she woke up.
sentences.zh: 我甚至觉得她都没有醒过来。

sentences.en: But in June's case, it didn't seem to help much.
sentences.zh: 但在朱恩的病例中，这似乎没有多大帮助。

sentences.en: And she and Lauren were still having problems breastfeeding afterwards.
sentences.zh: 事后她和劳伦在母乳喂养方面仍然有问题。

sentences.en: So while she's still in the hospital, she calls up the lactation consultant that she had hired, Melanie Henstrom, just to let her know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 因此，当她还在医院时，她打电话给她雇的哺乳顾问梅兰妮·亨斯特姆，只是为了让她知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And from talking to her on the phone, Melanie said that the situation was actually much worse than Lauren had thought and that Lauren's baby needed another tongue tie procedure,
sentences.zh: 通过电话交谈，梅兰妮说情况实际上比劳伦想象的要糟糕得多，劳伦的婴儿需要另一个舌系带手术，

sentences.en: a deeper cut under the tongue.
sentences.zh: 舌头下方的切口更深。

sentences.en: How did she make this diagnosis, Katie?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，她是怎么做出这个诊断的？

sentences.en: Was it over the phone?
sentences.zh: 是在电话里吗？

sentences.en: How did she know this?
sentences.zh: 她怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Lauren told us that it was from a phone conversation.
sentences.zh: 劳伦告诉我们，这是通过电话交谈得知的。

sentences.en: And in addition to that, she also warned her that basically, you know, Lauren and her husband should really take this seriously and consider getting it done.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，她还警告她说，基本上，你知道，劳伦和她的丈夫应该认真对待这一点并考虑去做。

sentences.en: Because if she doesn't get it fixed, it could lead to a whole host of problems beyond just problems breastfeeding.
sentences.zh: 因为如果不解决这个问题，除了母乳喂养的问题外，还可能导致一连串的问题。

sentences.en: Like, she'll have scoliosis and she'll suffer from migraines and she'll never eat and she'll have a speech impediment and she won't sleep.
sentences.zh: 比如，她会得脊柱侧弯，会遭受偏头痛折磨，永远不会吃饭，会有言语障碍，而且睡不好觉。

sentences.en: I mean, just like the long list of things over the phone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，电话里列出了一长串的事情。

sentences.en: And Lauren starts panicking.
sentences.zh: 劳伦开始惊慌失措。

sentences.en: I mean, first of all, I've never felt more terrible in my life than that first day or so after giving birth.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，生完孩子后的那一天左右，我从未感到如此糟糕。

sentences.en: Like, the come down from the hormones, the drugs, all of it, the sleep deprivation.
sentences.zh: 就像荷尔蒙消退、药物、这一切、睡眠剥夺。

sentences.en: And then, you know, here was this baby we'd wanted, we were told we probably would never have after one miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，这是我们一直想要的婴儿，我们被告知在流产一次后可能永远不会拥有。

sentences.en: And she's so perfect, like the most beautiful baby I'd ever seen.
sentences.zh: 她是如此完美，就像我见过的最美丽的婴儿。

sentences.en: And you think that she has some deformity that's going to ruin her.
sentences.zh: 你却认为她有什么会毁了她的畸形。

sentences.en: But Melanie says it's okay.
sentences.zh: 但梅兰妮说没关系。

sentences.en: You know, she has a solution and she tells Lauren that there's a dentist in town who can handle cases that are as severe as June's.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她有一个解决方案，她告诉劳伦城里有一位牙医可以处理像朱恩这么严重的病例。

sentences.en: A dentist?
sentences.zh: 牙医？

sentences.en: Why a dentist?
sentences.zh: 为什么是牙医？

sentences.en: Well, there's a procedure that's done in a dentist's office that's a laser surgery.
sentences.zh: 嗯，牙医诊所里有一种手术是激光手术。

sentences.en: And dentists use this high-powered laser machine that can quickly cut the flesh that connects the lips and the cheeks to the guMs.
sentences.zh: 牙医使用这种大功率激光机器，可以快速切割连接嘴唇和脸颊与牙龈的组织。

sentences.en: So according to Lauren, Melanie tells her that by chance, this dentist has an opening.
sentences.zh: 因此，据劳伦说，梅兰妮告诉她，这位牙医碰巧有一个空位。

sentences.en: Because she said a family coming in from Oregon had just canceled their Saturday appointment.
sentences.zh: 因为她说一个从俄勒冈州赶来的家庭刚刚取消了他们的周六预约。

sentences.en: So I thought, oh, okay, wow, you know, people are coming in from Oregon to see him.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，哦，好吧，哇，你知道，人们从俄勒冈州赶来找他看病。

sentences.en: And so we talked about it.
sentences.zh: 于是我们讨论了这件事。

sentences.en: We both felt unsure.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都感到很不确定。

sentences.en: But we said, well, let's at least take the appointment and then we can at least meet with the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们说，好吧，至少接受预约，然后我们至少可以见见牙医。

sentences.en: And also someone can look at our mouth and assess.
sentences.zh: 而且也有人可以看看我们的嘴并进行评估。

sentences.en: And so Lauren agrees to go in and meet the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 于是劳伦同意去见牙医。

sentences.en: Like I think some people, when they hear this story, think like, why would you believe that?
sentences.zh: 我想有些人听到这个故事时会想，你为什么会相信那个？

sentences.en: Like, it just sounds so scammy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太像骗局了。

sentences.en: But to me, there's a lot of things that you hear in the hospital that sound insane.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，你在医院里听到的很多事情听起来都很疯狂。

sentences.en: Like, it's no different than someone saying, like, your baby's orange because their Billy Reubens, their levers are too high.
sentences.zh: 这就像有人说，你的婴儿是橙色的，因为他们的胆红素、他们的肝脏太高了。

sentences.en: So we got to go put them under these lights.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得把他们放在这些灯光下。

sentences.en: Like, that sounds insane.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很疯狂。

sentences.en: That sounds more insane than, you know, your baby's having a hard time eating because their tongue is too tight and it needs to be cut.
sentences.zh: 这听起来比“你的婴儿因为舌头太紧而难以进食且需要被剪开”更疯狂。

sentences.en: Like, that seems rational, actually.
sentences.zh: 这看起来其实很合理。

sentences.en: And all of this seemed really weird to Lauren at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时所有这一切对劳伦来说都显得非常奇怪。

sentences.en: But, you know, in the context of the hospital and having a baby, lots of things about health care are weird.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在医院和生孩子的背景下，关于医疗保健的很多事情都很奇怪。

sentences.en: So one day after they got back home from the hospital, Lauren and her husband pack up the car and go to the office early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 因此，从医院回家的一天后，劳伦和丈夫收拾好车，一大早就去了诊所。

sentences.en: You know, I was wearing my hospital diaper and an ice pack.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我当时还戴着医院的产妇尿垫和冰敷袋。

sentences.en: Took the elevator up to his office.
sentences.zh: 坐电梯上了他的办公室。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Melanie greets them at the door.
sentences.zh: 梅兰妮在门口迎接了他们。

sentences.en: They signed some paperwork and pretty soon the dentist, Dr. Samuel Zink, arrives.
sentences.zh: 他们签了一些文件，很快牙医塞缪尔·津克医生就到了。

sentences.en: And then he, like, very briefly, you know, very briefly looks in her mouth and is like, yeah, she's got, you know, whatever, however he classified it.
sentences.zh: 然后他，你知道的，非常简单地，你知道的，非常简单地看了看她的嘴，然后就说，对啊，她有，你知道的，不管怎样，他就是那么分类的。

sentences.en: Grade four, whatever he says, class four.
sentences.zh: 四级，随便他怎么说，四级。

sentences.en: And she has a lip tie, which, you know, that had never been mentioned to us before.
sentences.zh: 她有唇系带过紧的问题，你知道的，这之前从来没人跟我们提过。

sentences.en: So it's very much like on the spot, like this new piece of information.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是当场决定的，像是一条全新的信息。

sentences.en: You know, pretty quickly, the dentist diagnosed June as having a couple of ties.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，没过多久，牙医就诊断出琼有几处系带过紧的问题。

sentences.en: He confirmed that she had a tongue tie and he said it was severe.
sentences.zh: 他确认她有舌系带过紧，并说情况很严重。

sentences.en: He also said that she had tightness under her top lip called a lip tie.
sentences.zh: 他还说她上嘴唇下方也很紧，被称为唇系带过紧。

sentences.en: And so the baby actually needed to get two cuts.
sentences.zh: 所以这个婴儿其实需要挨两刀。

sentences.en: And again, Lauren said that the dentist and the consultant told her how important it was for her to do this for her baby.
sentences.zh: 劳伦再次表示，牙医和顾问曾告诉她，为孩子做这个手术有多么重要。

sentences.en: One of us says, like, you know, what happens if we don't do the procedure?
sentences.zh: 我们其中一个人问，你知道的，如果我们不做这个手术会怎么样？

sentences.en: Like, what are our alternatives?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们有什么替代方案？

sentences.en: And it was like, basically, like, there's no alternative.
sentences.zh: 然后就基本上是，根本没有替代方案。

sentences.en: Like, you have to do this.
sentences.zh: 就像，你必须做这个。

sentences.en: Otherwise, like, again, long, long.
sentences.zh: 否则，就像我说的，很久很久。

sentences.en: So Lauren and her husband decided to do it.
sentences.zh: 于是劳伦和她丈夫决定做了。

sentences.en: But before the procedure starts, Melanie actually stopped Lauren from coming into the room.
sentences.zh: 但在手术开始前，梅兰妮居然阻止劳伦进房间。

sentences.en: Melanie turned around and put a hand on my shoulder and said, oh, no.
sentences.zh: 梅兰妮转过身，把手放在我的肩膀上说，哦，不行。

sentences.en: And I said, oh, am I not going with you?
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，我是不是不能跟你一起进去？

sentences.en: She goes, well, we can't tell you no, but, you know, if you hear her cry, it'll impact your milk supply.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，我们不能不让你进，但是，你知道的，如果你听到她哭，会影响你的奶水。

sentences.en: Like, adversely.
sentences.zh: 会有负面影响。

sentences.en: What do I know?
sentences.zh: 我懂什么呀？

sentences.en: So I said, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，哦，好吧。

sentences.en: And she pulled out the white noise machine and said, what do you want to listen to?
sentences.zh: 她拿出了白噪音机，问你想听什么？

sentences.en: And I had no idea what she was talking about.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道她在说什么。

sentences.en: I had no idea what it was.
sentences.zh: 我压根不知道那是什么东西。

sentences.en: And so then she just turned it on, white noise, and left.
sentences.zh: 然后她就把机器打开，放着白噪音，接着就出去了。

sentences.en: What happens next is Melanie turns on a white noise machine in the room.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事是，梅兰妮在房间里打开了一台白噪音机。

sentences.en: And that was the moment that I was like, get your baby and get out of here.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我心里想的是，快去把你的孩子抱走，离开这里。

sentences.en: And I didn't listen to it.
sentences.zh: 但我没有听从那种直觉。

sentences.en: It was like all of my mom intuition firing, being like, this isn't right, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像我所有的母亲直觉都在爆发，觉得这不对劲，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's like, I don't know how to describe it, but like a full body, you have to get your baby and get out of here.
sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，我无法形容，但那种全身心的感觉就是，你必须抱起你的孩子离开这里。

sentences.en: And I just ignored it.
sentences.zh: 而我却把这种感觉忽视了。

sentences.en: She said her maternal instincts really kicked in.
sentences.zh: 她说她的母性本能真的被激发了。

sentences.en: And she just had this instinctive fear about the procedure and whether June would be okay.
sentences.zh: 她对这个手术以及琼是否会没事产生了一种本能的恐惧。

sentences.en: But the procedure itself was very quick.
sentences.zh: 但手术本身非常快。

sentences.en: Within just a couple of minutes, Melanie returns with June.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几分钟后，梅兰妮抱着琼回来了。

sentences.en: And she was screaming.
sentences.zh: 她在尖叫。

sentences.en: Like, screaming.
sentences.zh: 简直是在尖叫。

sentences.en: And so worked up.
sentences.zh: 情绪激动到了极点。

sentences.en: This was like hysterical, inconsolable.
sentences.zh: 这简直是歇斯底里，无法安抚。

sentences.en: And she was also choking on something, like gagging.
sentences.zh: 而且她还被什么东西噎住了，一直在作呕。

sentences.en: And June was so worked up.
sentences.zh: 琼情绪激动得不得了。

sentences.en: Lauren had only had her for a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 劳伦把她接过来才不过几天。

sentences.en: But she said that this was on a different level than any other way she had ever seen June crying.
sentences.zh: 但她说，这跟她以前见过的琼哭闹的任何方式都完全不在一个级别。

sentences.en: And June just wouldn't stop crying.
sentences.zh: 而且琼就是停不下来地哭。

sentences.en: And she looked over to Melanie.
sentences.zh: 她看了看梅兰妮。

sentences.en: And Lauren said that she remembered Melanie saying this was very typical.
sentences.zh: 劳伦说她记得梅兰妮说过这非常典型。

sentences.en: And so they pay the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 于是他们付了牙医费。

sentences.en: They pay $600 for the procedure.
sentences.zh: 他们为这个手术付了600美元。

sentences.en: And then they go home.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就回家了。

sentences.en: And what happens?
sentences.zh: 结果呢？

sentences.en: Over the next several days, June did not get better, you know, as Melanie had assured them.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几天里，正如梅兰妮向他们保证的那样，琼并没有好转。

sentences.en: You know, she was basically inconsolable, Lauren said.
sentences.zh: 劳伦说，你知道的，她基本上无法被安抚。

sentences.en: Just crying hysterically.
sentences.zh: 只是歇斯底里地哭泣。

sentences.en: And Lauren and her husband, you know, they don't know how to comfort her.
sentences.zh: 劳伦和她丈夫，你知道的，根本不知道该怎么安慰她。

sentences.en: They're new parents.
sentences.zh: 他们是新手父母。

sentences.en: They've only had a baby a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 他们把孩子接回家才几天。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're almost beside themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们急得都快崩溃了。

sentences.en: There was nothing we could do.
sentences.zh: 我们什么也做不了。

sentences.en: And I remember finally I said, like, this is not normal.
sentences.zh: 我记得最后我说，这太不正常了。

sentences.en: We're going to the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 我们要去急诊室。

sentences.en: And they decide to go to the emergency room where a doctor looks inside June's mouth and finds a large sore in her mouth that he says is probably causing her so much pain.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定去急诊室，在那里医生看了看琼的嘴，发现她嘴里有一个很大的溃疡，医生说这可能让她感到了极大的痛苦。

sentences.en: And so he said, you know, it breaks my heart to see a sore that big in a baby this small.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，你知道的，看到这么小的婴儿嘴里有这么大的溃疡，我真的于心不忍。

sentences.en: It was like the floodgates opened and, like, there was nothing but guilt and shame.
sentences.zh: 就像闸门被打开了，铺天盖地全是负罪感和羞耻感。

sentences.en: Like, unmanageable guilt and shame.
sentences.zh: 那种无法承受的负罪感和羞耻感。

sentences.en: Like, what have we done?
sentences.zh: 就像，我们到底做了什么？

sentences.en: Who are these people?
sentences.zh: 这些人都是谁？

sentences.en: What have I done to my baby?
sentences.zh: 我对我的孩子做了什么？

sentences.en: Will she ever be the same?
sentences.zh: 她还能恢复正常吗？

sentences.en: Like, what did I do?
sentences.zh: 我到底干了什么？

sentences.en: So at this point, Lauren is really understanding that her intuition about this surgery was probably right and that she and her husband may have really made a mistake with this.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一刻，劳伦真正意识到，她对这次手术的直觉可能是对的，她和丈夫可能真的犯了个大错。

sentences.en: What does June's recovery look like?
sentences.zh: 琼的恢复情况怎么样？

sentences.en: So June never did end up breastfeeding successfully, which was the main reason why Lauren and her husband had decided to do this procedure.
sentences.zh: 所以琼最终并没有成功进行母乳喂养，而这正是劳伦和丈夫决定做这个手术的主要原因。

sentences.en: That was the whole point, right?
sentences.zh: 这才是全部的意义所在，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the whole point, right.
sentences.zh: 这才是全部的意义所在。

sentences.en: And over the next couple of years, June had a number of issues that, you know, there's no official medical diagnosis for,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，琼出现了一系列问题，你知道的，虽然没有官方的医学诊断，

sentences.en: but Lauren has attributed a lot of her behaviors to what had happened to her when she was just a few days old.
sentences.zh: 但劳伦把她的很多行为都归咎于她才几天大时所遭遇的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, you couldn't close a fridge door too loud or else it would, like, set her off.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你不能把冰箱门关得太大声，否则就会刺激到她。

sentences.en: Or, you know, we would attempt to take her for a stroller walk on the Greenbelt, which is the walking path.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我们尝试带她去绿化带（也就是那条步行小径）推婴儿车散步。

sentences.en: And she'd be asleep in her car seat, you know, stroller, and someone would try to pass us on their bike and, like, ring their bell.
sentences.zh: 她本来在汽车安全座椅或婴儿车里睡得好好的，然后有人骑着自行车试图从旁边经过，还按了铃。

sentences.en: And it would startle her and it would just, like, set her off.
sentences.zh: 这会吓到她，然后就会彻底刺激到她。

sentences.en: So she just was very, very, very fragile.
sentences.zh: 所以她变得非常非常非常脆弱。

sentences.en: So Lauren just wanted to get answers.
sentences.zh: 因此劳伦只想得到答案。

sentences.en: And she really wanted to hold Melanie and the dentist accountable.
sentences.zh: 她真的很想让梅兰妮和那个牙医承担责任。

sentences.en: So she gathered all of the paperwork that she had, texts, emails, other correspondence, and she went to the Idaho Board of Dentistry,
sentences.zh: 于是她收集了自己所有的文件、短信、电子邮件和其他信件，去找了爱达荷州牙科委员会，

sentences.en: where she filed a complaint against the dentiSt.
sentences.zh: 并在那里对该牙医提出了投诉。

sentences.en: And then she also went to a professional organization that certifies lactation consultants and filed a complaint with them as well.
sentences.zh: 然后她还去找了一个认证哺乳顾问的专业机构，并在那里也提出了投诉。

sentences.en: And did she get anywhere with either of them?
sentences.zh: 她找这两家机构有得到什么结果吗？

sentences.en: At first, no.
sentences.zh: 起初没有。

sentences.en: The Idaho Dentistry Board didn't want to investigate, and Lauren appealed, and she lost her appeal.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州牙科委员会不想调查，劳伦进行了申诉，但她的申诉被驳回了。

sentences.en: And she didn't initially hear back at all from the lactation board.
sentences.zh: 而且她最初根本没有收到哺乳期委员会的任何回复。

sentences.en: No one wanted to take responsibility.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意承担责任。

sentences.en: That's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里。

sentences.en: No one wanted to stick their neck out there.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意出头挑担子。

sentences.en: What's the alternative?
sentences.zh: 还有别的选择吗？

sentences.en: The story never gets told.
sentences.zh: 这个故事永远不会被讲出来。

sentences.en: And that's when she decided to reach out to us.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，她决定联系我们。

sentences.en: And after our story came out, the lactation board finally told Lauren that they were investigating Melanie.
sentences.zh: 我们的报道发表后，哺乳期委员会终于告诉劳伦，他们正在对梅兰妮进行调查。

sentences.en: And Katie, you guys were reporting the story.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，你们当时在做这篇报道。

sentences.en: I'm assuming you reached out to both the dentist and to Melanie.
sentences.zh: 我想你们一定联系了牙医和梅兰妮吧。

sentences.en: What did they say?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Beyond a very brief phone conversation that I had with Melanie, in which, you know, she defended her work and she said that she had a number of very satisfied customers,
sentences.zh: 除了我和梅兰妮有过一次非常简短的电话交谈外——在交谈中，你知道的，她为自己的工作进行了辩护，并称她有很多非常满意的客户——

sentences.en: she didn't respond to detailed questions about Lauren's story or the stories of her former clients.
sentences.zh: 她没有回应关于劳伦的故事或她前客户故事的详细提问。

sentences.en: And Dr. Zink did not respond to our request for comment.
sentences.zh: 津克医生没有回应我们的置评请求。

sentences.en: But he did tell the dentistry board that Lauren's baby's procedure was uneventful and that an extremely small percentage of patients do not respond well to the procedure.
sentences.zh: 但他确实对牙科委员会说，劳伦孩子的术后情况很平稳，只有极少数患者对该手术反应不佳。

sentences.en: And how big of an issue is this, Katie?
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，这个问题有多严重？

sentences.en: I mean, how common is it for mothers to have an experience like Lauren's?
sentences.zh: 我是说，母亲们有类似劳伦这种经历的情况有多普遍？

sentences.en: So, after we got the tip from Lauren and we dug deeper into her story, we found ourselves really surprised by how big this industry was for tongue-tie releases.
sentences.zh: 所以，在接到劳伦的线索并深入挖掘她的故事后，我们发现舌系带释放手术这个行业规模之大，实在让我们大吃一惊。

sentences.en: And in part, it's been driven by this movement for breastfeeding and the Breast is Best campaign and a growing number of parents who are choosing to breastfeed their children.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是由母乳喂养运动、“母乳最好”倡议以及越来越多的选择母乳喂养孩子的父母所推动的。

sentences.en: In turn, that has sparked this big boom in tongue-tie releases.
sentences.zh: 反过来，这也引发了舌系带释放手术的巨大热潮。

sentences.en: One study that we found showed that these procedures have grown 800% in recent years.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的一项研究表明，近年来这些手术增长了800%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: And also, as we started talking to other parents around the country, we learned that some of them had similar stories to what Lauren had told us.
sentences.zh: 而且，当我们开始与全国各地的其他父母交谈时，我们得知他们中的一些人也有着和劳伦告诉我们类似的经历。

sentences.en: There's plenty of instances where there's no harm done to the baby at all when they get these procedures.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多情况下，婴儿做这些手术时根本没有受到任何伤害。

sentences.en: But we also found cases where babies were harmed, you know, where they developed oral aversions,
sentences.zh: 但我们也发现了一些婴儿受到伤害的案例，你知道的，他们对口腔产生了抗拒，

sentences.en: which basically means that they don't want to eat because they fear having anything put in their mouth, including a bottle.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着他们不想吃东西，因为他们害怕任何东西放进嘴里，包括奶瓶。

sentences.en: We found cases where babies became malnourished, had to be hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 我们发现有婴儿营养不良、不得不入院治疗的案例。

sentences.en: We found more than one instance in which babies had to be given a feeding tube just weeks after the procedure.
sentences.zh: 我们发现不止一个案例表明，婴儿在手术后仅仅几周就被迫插上了鼻饲管。

sentences.en: So these sound so painful and awful for a newborn, these probleMs.
sentences.zh: 听起来这些问题对新生儿来说是如此痛苦和可怕。

sentences.en: But I guess, you know, there's always a risk, Katie, in any medical procedure, right?
sentences.zh: 但我想，你知道的，凯蒂，任何医疗手术总是有风险的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, how much of this is just the risk you sign up for when you agree that your baby should have a surgery?
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你同意让你的婴儿做手术时，这其中有多少仅仅是你自愿承担的风险？

sentences.en: Well, that's true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, there's always a risk.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，风险总是存在的。

sentences.en: But what you're supposed to do is weigh the risks against what the potential benefits of a procedure are.
sentences.zh: 但你本该做的是权衡风险与手术的潜在益处。

sentences.en: And when we really started drilling down into what those benefits were and into the medical research, we found there just wasn't a lot of potential benefit for these procedures,
sentences.zh: 当我们真正开始深入研究这些益处以及医学研究时，我们发现这些手术并没有带来太多的潜在益处，

sentences.en: you know, if at all in many cases.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在许多情况下甚至根本没有。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So the procedures don't have a medical reason to exist?
sentences.zh: 所以这些手术根本没有存在的医学依据？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We reviewed all of the best quality medical research on this.
sentences.zh: 我们查阅了关于此课题的所有最高质量的医学研究。

sentences.en: And, you know, other than that old-fashioned snip under the tongue, which does show that in some cases it can reduce pain for breastfeeding mothers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，除了舌头下方那种老式的剪开手术（确实表明在某些情况下可以减轻母乳喂养母亲的疼痛）之外，

sentences.en: But otherwise, all of this growth and all of these other more invasive procedures, we found there just wasn't good evidence that they help babies.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，所有这些增长以及所有其他更具侵入性的手术，我们发现根本没有充分的证据证明它们对婴儿有帮助。

sentences.en: And the more we looked into tongue ties and started to connect it to the other reporting we were doing,
sentences.zh: 而且我们对舌系带的研究越深入，并开始把它与我们正在做的其他报道联系起来时，

sentences.en: we started to realize that it was driven by some really big forces in our health care system that really had the potential to harm patients.
sentences.zh: 我们开始意识到，这是由我们医疗体系中一些非常强大的力量所驱动的，这些力量确实有可能对患者造成伤害。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的字谜游戏“Connections”。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com slash games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: So, Katie, we talked about this new surge in a procedure that surgically unties infants' tongues from the bottom of their mouths, often needlessly, sometimes even harmfully.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，我们谈到了最近一项激增的手术，即通过手术割开婴儿口底的舌系带，这通常是不必要的，有时甚至是有害的。

sentences.en: And you said your reporting found that this surgery was actually part of a broader trend.
sentences.zh: 你说你们的报道发现，这种手术实际上是一个更广泛趋势的一部分。

sentences.en: Tell me about this trend and what's driving it.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个趋势以及是什么在推动它。

sentences.en: So, that's what this investigation was really about, to find the procedures that are doing unnecessary harm to patients and to really kind of understand why this is happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是这项调查的真正目的，找出对患者造成不必要伤害的手术，并真正理解为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: You know, like what's driving the prevalence of these procedures.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如是什么推动了这些手术的流行。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's just a lot of unnecessary surgeries out there.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，外面有太多不必要的手术了。

sentences.en: But we decided to center our reporting on three particular surgeries that had the potential to harm patients in addition to tongue ties.
sentences.zh: 但除了舌系带手术之外，我们决定将报道中心放在另外三项有可能对患者造成伤害的特定手术上。

sentences.en: We focused on a particular hernia surgery, a bariatric surgery, which can be overdone and cause harm,
sentences.zh: 我们重点关注了一项特定的疝气手术、一项可能被过度实施并造成伤害的减重手术，

sentences.en: and a vascular surgery done on patients' legs to help us understand the forces that were at work that were driving all of this.
sentences.zh: 以及在患者腿部进行的血管手术，以帮助我们了解推动这一切的力量。

sentences.en: And what did you find when you dug deeper into those surgeries?
sentences.zh: 当你深入研究这些手术时，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's very complex, but we ultimately found three main drivers that were underlying all of these.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常复杂，但我们最终发现了所有这些现象背后的三个主要驱动因素。

sentences.en: First, there's a financial incentive for the doctors to perform these surgeries.
sentences.zh: 首先，医生进行这些手术有经济上的激励。

sentences.en: There's also a real push from the medical device companies that make these surgeries possible.
sentences.zh: 其次，制造这些手术所需设备的医疗器械公司也在大力推动。

sentences.en: And last, there's a huge information void for solid medical advice that a lot of these doctors and companies take advantage of in order to push the surgeries.
sentences.zh: 最后，可靠的医疗建议存在巨大的信息真空，许多医生和公司正是利用这一点来推销这些手术。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's start with the money, Katie.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯蒂，那我们先从金钱说起。

sentences.en: How exactly is that incentivizing doctors to perform a lot more of these procedures?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是如何激励医生做更多此类手术的？

sentences.en: Like, what are the mechanics of that?
sentences.zh: 比如，这其中的机制是什么？

sentences.en: So, the reality of our healthcare industry today is that in many places, you know, even in places like nonprofit hospitals, the doctors who work there are not getting a salary.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当今医疗保健行业的现实是，在许多地方，你知道的，甚至像非营利医院这样地方，在那里工作的医生是没有固定薪水的。

sentences.en: A straight salary, that's just kind of, you get paid for showing up to work that day.
sentences.zh: 直接拿固定薪水，那就有点像是，你那天去上班就能拿到报酬。

sentences.en: Instead, they're actually getting paid based on the procedures that they're doing, how complex those procedures are, possibly how lucrative.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们实际上是根据他们所做的手术、这些手术的复杂程度、可能还有它们的收益来获得报酬的。

sentences.en: And it's not every doctor.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个医生都这样。

sentences.en: There are still doctors that get paid salaries.
sentences.zh: 仍然有拿固定薪水的医生。

sentences.en: But it's increasingly the case that doctors have at least a part of their pay is tied to the procedures that they're doing.
sentences.zh: 但越来越普遍的情况是，医生的薪酬至少有一部分与他们所做的手术挂钩。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So, the procedure is growing in importance in terms of actual compensation for doctors.
sentences.zh: 因此，就医生的实际薪酬而言，手术的重要性越来越高。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, in part, it's kind of baked into the healthcare system that we've always had.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，这有点像是融入了我们一直以来拥有的医疗保健系统中。

sentences.en: You can even think about it as the small-town doctor who operated his own independent practice or her own independent practice.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以把它想象成经营自己独立诊所的小镇医生。

sentences.en: It's essentially a small business, and they would get paid based on the patients that they saw.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一个小型企业，他们会根据他们看诊的患者获得报酬。

sentences.en: But, like, increasingly, even in, for example, large hospital systems where you might think that a doctor is just getting paid a salary to work in a hospital.
sentences.zh: 但是，就像越来越普遍的那样，例如在大型医院系统中，你可能会认为医生在医院工作只是拿固定薪水。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, a chunk of their bonus, for example, can sometimes be tied to the procedures that they're doing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道的，例如他们奖金的一部分有时会与他们所做的手术挂钩。

sentences.en: And that is increasingly the case.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情况越来越普遍。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: And so, one particularly egregious example of this was at a hospital that's in New York, Bellevue Hospital.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中一个特别令人发指的例子发生在纽约的一家医院，贝尔维尤医院。

sentences.en: And basically, what my colleagues found there was that they had basically turned their surgery department into an assembly line for bariatric surgery,
sentences.zh: 基本上，我的同事在那里发现的是，他们基本上把他们的外科部门变成了减重手术的流水线，

sentences.en: which makes your stomach smaller and can lead to weight loss.
sentences.zh: 这会让你的胃变小，并能导致体重减轻。

sentences.en: But what we found was that they were green-lighting patients that basically didn't meet the qualifications for the surgery, which is a serious surgery.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现的是，他们对那些根本不符合该手术资格的患者亮起了绿灯，而这可是一项重大手术。

sentences.en: And what they found was that there were several situations where people had very serious outcomes as a result of getting the bariatric surgery there.
sentences.zh: 他们发现有几种情况下，人们在那里做完减重手术后产生了非常严重的后果。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is an extreme case of a hospital turning to a particular surgery to drive profits.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这是一个医院为了谋取利润而转向某项特定手术的极端案例。

sentences.en: And it wasn't uncommon in your reporting, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来在你们的报道中这并不罕见。

sentences.en: No, it wasn't the only example, but it was the most striking.
sentences.zh: 不，这不是唯一的例子，但却是最引人注目的。

sentences.en: And when we reached out to Bellevue, they defended their work, and they said that their practices were helping patients who wouldn't otherwise get care.
sentences.zh: 当我们联系贝尔维尤医院时，他们为自己的工作进行了辩护，并表示他们的做法是在帮助那些原本无法获得护理的患者。

sentences.en: But, you know, our reporting was pretty conclusive that the program was turning through a record number of surgeries.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们的报道相当确凿，该项目正在以前所未有的手术数量运转。

sentences.en: So, what else was driving this increase in harmful surgeries that you guys found?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们发现的导致这些有害手术增加的还有什么其他原因？

sentences.en: So, we found it wasn't just the hospitals who were benefiting.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们发现受益的不仅是医院。

sentences.en: The other major player that benefits are these companies that are making the tools and the products that doctors are using during the procedures.
sentences.zh: 另一个主要的受益者是那些制造医生在手术过程中使用的工具和产品的公司。

sentences.en: And in order for them to sell more of their products, a lot of time what they end up doing is promoting the procedures themselves.
sentences.zh: 为了销售更多产品，他们最终往往会去推广手术本身。

sentences.en: So, like medical device makers, like the company that made the laser in June's surgery.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像医疗器械制造商，比如琼手术中制造激光的那家公司。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, they do this in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们通过多种方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: They're giving them loans to help them buy the equipment, and in some cases, they're even lending them money to help set up those clinics where the procedures are performed.
sentences.zh: 他们向医生提供贷款以帮助他们购买设备，在某些情况下，他们甚至借钱给他们来建立开展手术的诊所。

sentences.en: So, they're really underwriting these doctors so that they can perform more surgeries and ultimately sell more machines.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们实际上是在为这些医生提供资金支持，以便他们能够进行更多手术，并最终销售更多机器。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the other things that they do is, you know, the laser companies, for example,
sentences.zh: 他们做的另一件事是，你知道的，例如激光公司，

sentences.en: they will host webinars where they will have dentists who frequently perform these procedures show other dentists how to do the procedures.
sentences.zh: 他们会举办网络研讨会，邀请经常做这些手术的牙医向其他牙医展示如何做这些手术。

sentences.en: We even discovered this conference that was created by one of the laser companies, and it had kind of a wild name.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至发现了其中一家激光公司创建的一个会议，它的名字有点疯狂。

sentences.en: The name of the conference was Tongue Ties and Tequilas.
sentences.zh: 那个会议的名字叫“舌系带与龙舌兰酒”。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It brought in dentists to talk about how to make money off the procedures, you know, how to promote themselves on social media, how to actually perform the procedure.
sentences.zh: 它把牙医们聚集在一起，讨论如何从这些手术中赚钱，你知道的，如何在社交媒体上宣传自己，如何实际执行手术。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, when they were all done, they got to celebrate with an open tequila bar.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当然当他们都忙完后，他们可以去开放式的龙舌兰酒吧庆祝。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, a lot of this really amounts to these companies trying to popularize these procedures, basically, like to get the word out,
sentences.zh: 所以，这在很大程度上意味着这些公司试图将这些手术大众化，基本上就是把消息传出去，

sentences.en: even if the procedures don't really work or in some cases cause harm.
sentences.zh: 即使这些手术并不真的管用，或者在某些情况下会造成伤害。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But they also play a big role in the other factor that's driving a lot of this, which is the information that they put out there about the surgeries.
sentences.zh: 但他们在另一个推动这一切的因素中也扮演着重要角色，那就是他们发布的关于这些手术的信息。

sentences.en: These companies often sponsor research, which doctors often rely on to guide their practices.
sentences.zh: 这些公司经常赞助研究，医生们往往依赖这些研究来指导他们的临床实践。

sentences.en: And, you know, part of what we found is that it can kind of create this echo chamber where doctors feel more comfortable and justified in doing these procedures
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们发现的一部分是，这会营造出一种回音室效应，让医生在进行这些手术时感到更安心、更有正当理由，

sentences.en: when they have kind of this whole alternate universe that is telling them that it's okay to do these procedures.
sentences.zh: 当他们拥有这样一个向他们灌输做这些手术没问题的整个平行世界时。

sentences.en: And, in fact, it's beneficial to patients.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上，这对患者是有益的。

sentences.en: So, tell me about this echo chamber effect.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟我讲讲这种回音室效应。

sentences.en: The best example of this we found was a doctor in Michigan named Dr. Jihad Mustafa.
sentences.zh: 我们找到的这方面的最佳例子是密歇根州的一位医生，名叫吉哈德·穆斯塔法医生。

sentences.en: He calls himself the leg saver.
sentences.zh: 他自称是救腿者。

sentences.en: And what we found was that he and several other doctors do these procedures called atherectomies,
sentences.zh: 我们发现他和几位其他医生在做一种叫做斑块切除术的手术，

sentences.en: which is basically like inserting a tiny roto-rooter inside an artery to get the blood flowing.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像是在动脉里插入一个微型管道疏通器来让血液流通。

sentences.en: Dr. Mustafa, in particular, was not only a very prolific performer of these procedures,
sentences.zh: 穆斯塔法医生不仅是这类手术的多产执行者，

sentences.en: but he actually founded his own medical conference and even helped start a medical journal that was devoted to using these procedures.
sentences.zh: 而且他还创立了自己的医疗会议，甚至帮助创办了一本专门致力于使用这些手术的医学期刊。

sentences.en: And, you know, like tongue ties, there's really no good evidence that these are actually beneficial to patients.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，就像舌系带一样，实在没有好的证据证明这些对患者真的有益。

sentences.en: And, in fact, despite his nickname as the leg saver,
sentences.zh: 事实上，尽管他有着救腿者的绰号，

sentences.en: one insurance company told Michigan authorities that 45 people had lost their limbs after getting treated at Dr. Mustafa's clinic over a four-year period.
sentences.zh: 一家保险公司曾向密歇根当局透露，在四年时间里，有45人在穆斯塔法医生的诊所接受治疗后失去了肢体。

sentences.en: Forty-five people lost their limbs?
sentences.zh: 四十五人失去了肢体？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that is the ultimate version of harm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是伤害的终极形式。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, he did speak to us and he defended his work and said that he treats very sick people.
sentences.zh: 现在，他确实跟我们谈过，并为自己的工作进行了辩护，称他治疗的都是病情非常严重的患者。

sentences.en: And despite his best efforts, some of these patients are, you know, already so sick that they sometimes lose their limbs.
sentences.zh: 尽管他尽了最大努力，但其中一些患者，你知道的，病情已经严重到有时会失去肢体。

sentences.en: And how much did he receive for each procedure?
sentences.zh: 他每次手术能获得多少报酬？

sentences.en: Doctors like him typically receive about $13,000 for each of these atherectomy procedures.
sentences.zh: 像他这样的医生每次进行此类斑块切除术通常能获得约1.3万美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But we found that that misinformation or poor information also applied when doctors were learning new types of surgeries.
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，当医生学习新类型的手术时，这种错误信息或不良信息同样适用。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Like how?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: So one of the areas we looked at was the area of hernia surgery that I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我们研究的领域之一就是我提到的疝气手术领域。

sentences.en: And there's a particular type of surgery, it's a very complex version of a hernia surgery called component separation.
sentences.zh: 有一种特定类型的手术，它是疝气手术中一种非常复杂的版本，叫做组分分离术。

sentences.en: And the expert surgeons that we spoke to said that it's difficult to learn and you have to practice it over and over and over again to get it right.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的专家外科医生说，这很难学，你必须一遍又一遍地练习才能掌握它。

sentences.en: But one recent survey of hernia surgeons said that one out of the four surgeons had taught themselves how to perform that operation.
sentences.zh: 但最近对疝气外科医生的一项调查显示，四分之一的外科医生是自学如何进行该手术的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not by learning it from an experienced surgeon, but by watching videos on Facebook and YouTube.
sentences.zh: 不是向有经验的外科医生学习，而是通过观看脸书和油管上的视频。

sentences.en: I mean, how unusual is that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有多罕见？

sentences.en: I guess to me it strikes me as very unusual.
sentences.zh: 我想对我来说，这让人觉得非常罕见。

sentences.en: I mean, I think of, you know, learning about how to take my kitchen faucet apart on YouTube, but I do not think of a doctor learning about how to perform a surgery on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想象的是，你知道的，在油管上学习如何拆卸我的厨房水龙头，但我不会想到医生在油管上学习如何做手术。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, it has actually become increasingly popular in recent years, and there's not good vetting of the quality of the instruction.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，近年来它实际上越来越受欢迎，并且对教学质量的审查并不严格。

sentences.en: We even found videos on a website run by a medical device company that was intended to be a how-to for how to do these surgeries, but the video contained serious mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至在一个由医疗器械公司运营的网站上找到了视频，这些视频本意是作为如何做这些手术的操作指南，但视频中包含严重的错误。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And, Katie, all of these videos, some of them with serious mistakes, I mean, is this something that would be subject to medical regulators?
sentences.zh: 而且，凯蒂，所有这些视频，其中一些还带有严重的错误，我的意思是，这会受到医疗监管机构的管辖吗？

sentences.en: Like, is there any kind of rules of the road for this stuff?
sentences.zh: 比如，这方面有什么行业规则吗？

sentences.en: You know, there's less than you would expect.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比你想象的要少。

sentences.en: Sometimes hospitals have rules about what sort of education their doctors need before performing a surgery,
sentences.zh: 有时医院对医生在做手术前需要什么样的教育有规定，

sentences.en: but we were surprised that there was a lot less regulation than we thought there would be, and much less vetting of these videos than we anticipated.
sentences.zh: 但我们惊讶地发现，监管比我们想象的要少得多，对这些视频的审查也比我们预期的要少得多。

sentences.en: So essentially what you found was this complex, oftentimes interconnected group of forces, device companies pushing their products,
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上发现的是一个复杂且往往相互关联的力量群体，推销产品的器械公司，

sentences.en: hospitals bolstering their bottom line, and rampant misinformation that, as you said, all really trace back to the same motivating factor, which is money.
sentences.zh: 巩固底线的医院，以及正如你所说，所有这些实际上都可以追溯到同一个动机——金钱的猖獗错误信息。

sentences.en: But wouldn't the fear of being sued for medical malpractice prevent a lot of this behavior?
sentences.zh: 但是，对医疗事故起诉的恐惧难道不能阻止这种行为吗？

sentences.en: You know, this kept popping up during the course of our reporting.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在我们的报道过程中，这个问题一直不断出现。

sentences.en: I do think we have this idea that anytime a doctor does anything wrong, they're going to get sued.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为我们有这样一种想法，即只要医生做了错事，他们就会被起诉。

sentences.en: But that just wasn't always the case in our reporting.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的报道中，情况并非总是如此。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of statutes of limitations, time limits on when somebody can file a lawsuit, and other ways that make it somewhat hard to really hold a doctor accountable.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有很多诉讼时效，对某人提起诉讼的时间限制，以及其他一些使得真正追究医生责任变得有点困难的方法。

sentences.en: One example is the regulatory organizations that oversee doctors.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是监督医生的监管组织。

sentences.en: The one doctor that I mentioned earlier, Dr. Mustafa, state investigators had found that his overuse of procedures had led people to lose their legs.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到的那位医生，穆斯塔法医生，州调查人员发现他对手术的过度使用导致人们失去了双腿。

sentences.en: And yet, he ultimately settled with the state, and he was fined $25,000.
sentences.zh: 然而，他最终与州里达成和解，被罚款2.5万美元。

sentences.en: That actually adds up to about two of these atherectomy procedures.
sentences.zh: 这实际上加起来也就相当于两次这样的斑块切除手术。

sentences.en: So it sounds like malpractice is not necessarily going to be the route to rectifying a lot of this.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来医疗过失诉讼不一定会成为纠正这一切的途径。

sentences.en: But I guess I'm wondering if the federal government could actually rein some of this in, you know, before the patients are harmed.
sentences.zh: 但我想我在想，联邦政府是否真的能在患者受到伤害之前遏制其中一些行为。

sentences.en: You know, it's possible, but this is just a very difficult issue.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是可能的，但这确实是一个非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Some of the themes that we explored in this reporting are really just firmly embedded in our healthcare system and the way that it works.
sentences.zh: 我们在这次报道中探讨的一些主题实际上已经深深植根于我们的医疗保健系统及其运作方式中。

sentences.en: The fact is that we have a for-profit healthcare system, right?
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们拥有一个营利性的医疗保健系统，对吧？

sentences.en: So everyone from doctors to hospitals to the device companies benefit when more procedures are done.
sentences.zh: 因此，从医生到医院再到器械公司，每个人都在进行更多手术时受益。

sentences.en: All of the incentives are pointing in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 所有的激励措施都指向同一个方向。

sentences.en: And so trying to find one or two simple solutions will probably not easily fix the issue, as much as we all hope that it could.
sentences.zh: 因此，试图找到一两个简单的解决方案可能无法轻易解决这个问题，尽管我们所有人都希望它能。

sentences.en: So is the lesson here being much more discriminating and vigilant as a patient?
sentences.zh: 所以这里的教训是作为患者要更有辨别力、更加警惕吗？

sentences.en: I mean, to get a second opinion when you're standing in front of a doctor or a dentist who's telling you that you or your baby needs a procedure?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你面对一个告诉你你或你的宝宝需要做手术的医生或牙医时，要去寻求第二诊疗意见？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that is one of the takeaways.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是要点之一。

sentences.en: But look,
sentences.zh: 但听着，

sentences.en: we understood that even reporting on all of this was risky because people could hear about these harmful surgeries and start wondering if everything that their doctors tells them is a scam.
sentences.zh: 我们明白，甚至连报道所有这些都是有风险的，因为人们可能会听到这些有害的手术，并开始怀疑医生告诉他们的每一件事是不是都是骗局。

sentences.en: And of course, while some of these procedures are harmful, a lot of procedures are life-saving.
sentences.zh: 当然，虽然其中一些手术是有害的，但许多手术是可以挽救生命的。

sentences.en: But ultimately, for now, patients are kind of left on their own to navigate what's a pretty complex and opaque healthcare system.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，目前患者只能靠自己去应对这个相当复杂且不透明的医疗保健系统。

sentences.en: When you have somebody standing in front of you saying, you should do this, it can be very confusing.
sentences.zh: 当有人站在你面前说，你应该这样做时，这可能会非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is something that Lauren talked a lot about, just how confusing all of this was for her.
sentences.zh: 这也是劳伦经常谈论的事情，关于这一切对她来说是多么令人困惑。

sentences.en: There's a lot of information that you're getting that is truly like someone is speaking a foreign language.
sentences.zh: 你得到的很多信息真的就像有人在说一门外语。

sentences.en: And because they do it all day long, it's not user-friendly.
sentences.zh: 因为他们整天都在这样做，所以它并不对用户友好。

sentences.en: Like, it isn't designed for the comfort or understanding of the person receiving the information.
sentences.zh: 就像，它不是为了接受信息的人的舒适度或理解力而设计的。

sentences.en: There is so much blind trust and faith that you have in the system, in the providers who are giving this information.
sentences.zh: 你对这个系统、对提供这些信息的医疗服务提供者有着太多的盲目信任和信仰。

sentences.en: You trust, like, this is what they do all day long.
sentences.zh: 你相信，这就是他们一整天都在做的事情。

sentences.en: So there is no real reason to question.
sentences.zh: 所以没有真正的理由去质疑。

sentences.en: That is the system that we have in this country.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在这个国家拥有的系统。

sentences.en: Katie, thank you.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
